column1: 8:1|“At that time,” declares the **LORD**, “the bones of Judah’s kings and officials, the bones of the priests and prophets, and the bones of Jerusalem’s inhabitants will be brought out of their graves.|Retains all five groups and repeated bones; reads recorded plural verb without identifying the agents.

8:2|They will be spread out before the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven—the ones they loved, served, followed, sought, and bowed down to. The bones will not be gathered or buried. They will lie like dung on the ground.|Keeps the five worship verbs and shame of unburied remains before the objects of devotion.

8:3|All who remain of this evil family will prefer death to life, wherever I have driven the survivors,” declares the **LORD** of hosts.|Preserves exile and survivors without smoothing the stated preference for death.

8:4|“Tell them: This is what the **LORD** says:\nWhen people fall, don’t they get up?\nWhen someone turns away, doesn’t that person turn back?|Makes generic subjects clear while retaining paired questions and turn wordplay.

8:5|Then why has this people turned away—
Jerusalem—in a lasting refusal to return?
They cling to deceit;
they refuse to turn back.|Keeps Jerusalem’s apposition and repeated return language.

8:6|I have listened closely,
but they do not speak honestly.
No one regrets their evil
and asks, ‘What have I done?’
Everyone returns to their own course,
like a horse charging into battle.|Follows recorded course reading and retains self-question and battle image.

8:7|Even the stork in the sky knows its appointed seasons;
the turtledove, swift, and crane
keep the time of their return.
But my people do not know
the **LORD**’s judgment.|Retains four birds, recorded swift reading, and contrast with divine judgment.

8:8|How can you say, ‘We are wise;
the **LORD**’s instruction is with us’?
Look—the lying pen of the scribes
has turned it into a lie.|Keeps challenge to scribal handling of instruction; does not expand into a theory of scripture.

8:9|The wise are put to shame,
shattered and trapped.
They have rejected the **LORD**’s word;
what wisdom do they have?|Preserves rejection as basis of the rhetorical wisdom question.

8:10|So I will give their wives to others
and their fields to new owners.
From the least to the greatest,
everyone is greedy for gain.
From prophet to priest,
everyone deals in lies.|Retains gender-specific threatened dispossession and both social ranges.

8:11|They treat the wound of my daughter, my people,
as though it were slight,
saying, ‘Peace, peace,’
when there is no peace.|Retains personified daughter and repeated peace rather than flattening to reassurance.

8:13|“I will sweep them away,” declares the **LORD**.
“No grapes on the vine,
no figs on the fig tree;
the leaves have withered.
What I gave them will pass away from them.”|Adopts removal sense in difficult gathering verb and states uncertainty about last clause in note.

8:14|“Why are we sitting here?
Gather together!
Let’s enter the fortified cities
and perish there.
For the **LORD** our God has doomed us
and given us poisoned water to drink,
because we sinned against the **LORD**.|Retains collective speech, repeated divine names, and destruction sense of silence verb.
8:15|We hoped for peace, but no good came;\nfor a time of healing, but look—terror!”|Keeps peace/healing hopes and abrupt terror.

8:16|From Dan comes the snorting of his horses;
at the neighing of his stallions,
the whole land trembles.
They come and devour the land and all it holds,
the city and those who live in it.|Leaves unnamed enemy possessive intact; preserves Dan and total devastation.

8:17|“Look, I am sending snakes among you,\nadders that cannot be charmed.\nThey will bite you,” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps serpent attack as divine speech, without turning it into an explicit allegory.
8:18|My comfort fails in sorrow;\nmy heart is sick within me.|Uses tentative comfort sense of rare expression; note marks uncertainty and speaker ambiguity.

8:19|Listen! My daughter, my people, cries out
from a distant land:
‘Is the **LORD** no longer in Zion?
Is her king no longer there?’
‘Why have they provoked me with their carved images,
with foreign things of emptiness?’|Keeps voices distinct through quotation and preserves idols as empty things.
8:20|“The harvest is past,\nthe summer is over,\nand we have not been saved.”|Preserves compact seasonal lament without interpreting rescue timing.
8:21|At the breaking of my daughter, my people, I am broken.\nI mourn;\nhorror has taken hold of me.|Preserves shared breaking language and mourning voice.

8:22|Is there no balm in Gilead?
Is there no healer there?
Why, then, has healing not come
to my daughter, my people?|Retains three questions and regional healing image rather than answering them.

8:23|If only my head were water
and my eyes a spring of tears!
I would weep day and night
for the slain of my daughter, my people.|Retains repository Hebrew 8:23 label and embodied unending lament; common English numbering places this at 9:1.

9:1|If only I had a travelers’ shelter in the wilderness!
I would leave my people
and go away from them.
For they are all adulterers,
a gathering of traitors.|Retains repository Hebrew 9:1 label and desire to leave the adulterous gathering; common English numbering places this at 9:2.

9:2|“They bend their tongues like bows;
lies, not faithfulness, prevail in the land.
They go from one evil to another
and do not know me,” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps tongue-bow image and failure to know God without identifying a human speaker.

9:3|“Beware of your neighbor;
do not trust any brother.
Every brother is a schemer,
and every neighbor spreads slander.|Retains brother alongside neighbor and notes Jacob-like verbal wordplay.

9:4|They deceive one another
and do not speak the truth.
They have trained their tongues to lie;
they wear themselves out doing wrong.|Keeps learned lying and exhausting wrongdoing rather than moral paraphrase.
9:5|You live surrounded by deceit.\nIn their deceit they refuse to know me,”\ndeclares the **LORD**.|Retains singular you and plural their without forced speaker identification.

9:6|So this is what the **LORD** of hosts says:
“Look, I will refine them and test them.
What else can I do
because of my daughter, my people?|Keeps refining/testing and difficult motivating question.

9:7|Their tongue is a deadly arrow;
it speaks deceit.
With the mouth, someone speaks peace to a neighbor,
while inwardly laying an ambush.|Uses deadly sense of arrow adjective with written/read uncertainty noted.

9:8|Should I not call them to account for this?”
declares the **LORD**.
“Should I not avenge myself
on a nation like this?|Retains repeated judgment questions and personal divine vengeance.

9:9|I will lift up weeping and wailing over the mountains,
a lament over the wilderness pastures.
They are burned out; no one passes through.
No sound of livestock is heard.
Birds of the sky and animals alike
have fled and gone.|Preserves first-person lament and animal loss, without overassigning speaker.

9:10|I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins,
a home for jackals.
I will make Judah’s cities desolate,
with no one living there.”|Keeps divine devastation and concrete jackal habitation.

9:11|Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the **LORD** spoken, so that they can explain it? Why has the land perished, burned out like a wilderness where no one passes?|Keeps three linked questions and asks for an explanation rather than supplying one early.

9:12|The **LORD** said, “Because they abandoned my instruction, which I set before them. They did not listen to my voice or walk in it.|Keeps instruction, hearing, and walking as linked covenant images.
9:13|Instead, they followed their stubborn hearts and the Baals, as their fathers taught them.”|Preserves fathers as transmitters and plural Baals.

9:14|So this is what the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, says: “Look, I am feeding this people wormwood and giving them poisoned water to drink.|Retains food and drink judgment images without substituting abstract suffering.

9:15|I will scatter them among nations neither they nor their fathers knew. I will send the sword after them until I have brought them to an end.”|Retains unfamiliar exile destinations and full force of threatened destruction.
9:16|This is what the **LORD** of hosts says:\n“Consider this: call the mourning women; let them come.\nSend for the skilled women; let them come.|Keeps female specialists and repeated summons.
9:17|Let them hurry and lift up a wail over us,\nso our eyes stream with tears\nand our eyelids flow with water.|Preserves plural us and embodied mourning without correcting speaker shift.

9:18|For a voice of wailing is heard from Zion:
‘How we have been devastated!
How deeply we are ashamed!
We have left the land;
our homes have been torn down.’|Chooses destruction sense for difficult dwelling clause; note retains displacement alternative.

9:19|Women, hear the **LORD**’s word;
let your ears receive what his mouth says.
Teach your daughters to wail,
and one another to lament.|Keeps female address and transmission of lament across generations.

9:20|Death has climbed through our windows
and entered our palaces,
to cut off children from the street
and young men from the squares.|Retains personified intruding Death and age/gender-specific victims.

9:21|Say: ‘This is what the **LORD** declares:
Human corpses will fall like dung on the open field,
like cut grain behind the reaper,
with no one to gather it.’”|Retains unburied corpses and agricultural image without euphemism.

9:22|This is what the **LORD** says:
“Let the wise not boast in their wisdom,
the strong not boast in their strength,
or the rich boast in their riches.|Keeps three parallel prohibitions and root repetitions.

9:23|Let anyone who boasts boast in this:
that they understand and know me,
that I am the **LORD**, who acts with steadfast love,
justice, and righteousness on earth.
For these are what delight me,”
declares the **LORD**.|Retains knowing God and three consequential biblical terms; both names retained.

9:24|“Look, days are coming,” declares the **LORD**, “when I will call to account all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised—|Preserves deliberately paradoxical circumcision language and continuing list.

9:25|Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the edges of their hair and live in the wilderness. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”|Retains Judah in list, hair practice, and bodily/heart contrast without harmonization.
10:1|House of Israel, hear the word the **LORD** has spoken about you.|Keeps collective Israel address and divine speech.

10:2|This is what the **LORD** says:
“Do not learn the way of the nations
or be terrified by signs in the sky,
though the nations are terrified by them.|Retains signs and nations contrast without importing astrology details into text.
10:3|The peoples’ customs are emptiness.\nSomeone cuts a tree from the forest;\na craftworker shapes it with a tool.|Keeps emptiness image and human manufacture; tool identification remains broad.
10:4|They adorn it with silver and gold,\nfasten it with nails and hammers\nso it will not wobble.|Preserves material sequence and dependence on fastening.

10:5|Like scarecrows in a cucumber field,
they cannot speak.
They must be carried, because they cannot walk.
Do not fear them:
they can do no harm,
and they have no power to do good.”|Uses field-scarecrow reading with alternative noted; retains both limits of agency.
10:6|No one is like you, **LORD**.\nYou are great;\nyour name is great in might.|Preserves direct prayer and repeated greatness.

10:7|Who would not fear you, King of the nations?
It is your due.
Among all the nations’ wise ones
and throughout their kingdoms,
no one is like you.|Keeps universal kingship and fear due to God without changing it to admiration.
10:8|All together they are senseless and foolish;\nthe instruction of empty idols is only wood.|Keeps sharp equation of idol instruction with wood; note acknowledges compressed syntax.

10:9|Beaten silver comes from Tarshish
and gold from Uphaz,
the work of a craftworker and a goldsmith’s hands.
Blue and purple are their clothing;
all of it is skilled workers’ handiwork.|Retains pinned Uphaz, trade materials, colors, and workmanship.

10:11|This is what you are to tell them: “The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will vanish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.”|Translates the Aramaic sentence directly; preserves make/vanish wordplay in note rather than invented rhyme.
10:12|He made the earth by his power,\nestablished the world by his wisdom,\nand stretched out the heavens by his understanding.|Keeps three creation actions and corresponding attributes.

10:13|When he gives voice, waters roar in the heavens.
He raises clouds from the ends of the earth,
makes lightning for the rain,
and brings wind out of his storehouses.|Keeps heavenly water and storehouse imagery; reads recorded definite earth.
10:15|They are emptiness, objects of mockery.\nWhen they are called to account, they will perish.|Preserves emptiness and visitation language without giving idols actual divinity.

10:16|Jacob’s portion is not like these,
for he is the one who forms everything.
Israel is the tribe of his inheritance;
the **LORD** of hosts is his name.|Retains mutual portion/inheritance relationship and divine title.
10:17|Gather your bundle from the ground,\nyou who live under siege.|Follows recorded feminine resident and retains urgent packing image.

10:18|For this is what the **LORD** says:
“This time I am slinging out the land’s inhabitants.
I will press them hard,
so that they feel it.”|Retains sling metaphor and difficult find clause with note rather than unsupported detailed outcome.

10:19|Oh, my brokenness!
My wound is severe.
Yet I said, “This is my sickness,
and I must bear it.”|Keeps lament and self-address; does not force identification of personified speaker.

10:20|My tent is destroyed;
all its ropes are snapped.
My children have gone from me and are no more.
There is no one left to pitch my tent
or hang its curtains.|Retains tent family image and ambiguous absence/death of children.

10:21|The shepherds have become senseless
and have not sought the **LORD**.
So they have not prospered,
and their whole flock is scattered.|Keeps shepherd metaphor and causal failure without naming a modern institution.

10:22|Listen—a report is coming!
A great uproar from the northern land,
to turn Judah’s cities into a wasteland,
a home for jackals.|Preserves unnamed northern threat and repeated jackal image.
10:23|I know, **LORD**, that people do not own their way;\nthose who walk cannot direct their own steps.|Keeps road/steps image and generic human scope.
10:24|Correct me, **LORD**, but with justice,\nnot in your anger,\nor you will reduce me to nothing.|Retains request for correction and justice rather than immunity.

10:25|Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you,
on the families that do not call on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob—
devoured him and consumed him—
and laid waste his home.|Preserves harsh prayer and repeated devouring rather than toning down vengeance.
11:1|The word that came to Jeremiah from the **LORD**:|Retains prophetic introduction without adding a historical date.

11:2|“Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.|Keeps plural hear and singular commission in English without inventing the audience’s identity.
11:3|Tell them: This is what the **LORD**, Israel’s God, says: Cursed is anyone who does not listen to the words of this covenant,|Preserves covenant curse and continuing sentence.

11:4|which I commanded your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, ‘Listen to my voice and do everything I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God.’|Retains iron furnace and reciprocal covenant formula.

11:5|This was to fulfill the oath I swore to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today.” I answered, “Amen, **LORD**.”|Keeps oath, inherited land image, and prophet’s audible response.
11:6|The **LORD** said to me, “Proclaim all these words in Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s streets: Hear the words of this covenant and do them!|Retains public locations and hearing-to-doing link.

11:7|From the day I brought your ancestors up from Egypt until today, I warned them insistently, again and again: ‘Listen to my voice.’|Renders early-rising idiom as repeated urgency rather than literal schedule.

11:8|But they did not listen or incline their ears. Each followed the stubbornness of their evil heart. So I brought on them all the terms of this covenant, which I commanded them to carry out, but they did not.”|Keeps listening image and consequences as covenant terms, not an added curse list.
11:9|The **LORD** said to me, “A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.|Preserves conspiracy charge and both locations.

11:10|They have returned to the sins of their forefathers, who refused to hear my words. They have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their ancestors.|Keeps return-to-sin contrast and names both houses.

11:11|So this is what the **LORD** says: Look, I am bringing a disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.|Preserves troubling refusal of prayer without softening.

11:12|Then Judah’s cities and Jerusalem’s inhabitants will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn offerings. But those gods will certainly not save them in their time of disaster.|Makes divine referent clear and retains emphatic inability to save.

11:13|Judah, you have as many gods as cities. You have set up as many altars to Shame as there are streets in Jerusalem—altars for burning offerings to Baal.|Preserves numerical comparison and derogatory Shame designation explained by Baal.

11:14|As for you, do not pray for this people or lift up a cry or prayer for them. I will not listen when they call to me because of their disaster.|Keeps direct prohibition to prophet and repeated prayer language.

11:15|What is my beloved doing in my house
while so many carry out wicked schemes?
Sacred meat will pass away from you;
you rejoice in your evil.|Retains difficult pinned clause without silently replacing consonants; note records uncertainty.

11:16|The **LORD** called you
‘A flourishing olive tree, beautiful with fine fruit.’
With the sound of a great roar,
he set it on fire,
and its branches were broken.|Keeps named olive image and sudden destruction; avoids overidentifying the roar.

11:17|The **LORD** of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you because of the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah did, provoking me by burning offerings to Baal.”|Preserves planter/judgment relation and third-to-first divine speech shift.
11:18|The **LORD** made it known to me, and I knew. Then you showed me what they were doing.|Retains third-to-second person address and knowledge repetition.

11:19|I was like a tame lamb led to slaughter. I did not know they were plotting against me: “Let’s destroy the tree with its fruit! Let’s cut him off from the land of the living, so his name is remembered no more.”|Keeps innocent lamb and conspirators’ tree metaphor; fruit sense of food noted.

11:20|But **LORD** of hosts, you judge justly
and test the innermost being and heart.
Let me see your vengeance on them,
for I have laid my case before you.|Retains legal plea and vengeance; kidneys image explained in note.

11:21|So this is what the **LORD** says about the men of Anathoth who seek your life and say, “Do not prophesy in the **LORD**’s name, or you will die by our hands.”|Keeps hometown threat, specific men, and both divine names.

11:22|This is what the **LORD** of hosts says: “Look, I am calling them to account. Their young men will die by the sword; their sons and daughters will die of hunger.|Retains age and gender distinctions and severe punishment.
11:23|No remnant will remain for them, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year they are called to account.”|Keeps no-remnant claim without harmonizing with later restoration.

12:1|You are righteous, **LORD**,
when I bring my case before you.
Still, I want to speak with you about justice.
Why does the way of the wicked prosper?
Why do all the treacherous live at ease?|Keeps acknowledgment and genuine challenge together; no apologetic answer added.

12:2|You planted them, and they took root.
They grow and bear fruit.
You are near in their mouths
but far from their innermost being.|Retains divine responsibility in planting and mouth/inward contrast.

12:4|How long will the land mourn
and the grass in every field wither?
Because of the evil of those who live there,
animals and birds are swept away.
For they say, ‘He will not see what happens to us.’|Retains ecological harm and ambiguous he; note gives uncertainty.

12:5|“If racing against people on foot has worn you out,
how will you compete with horses?
If you feel secure in a peaceful land,
how will you manage in the Jordan’s thickets?|Keeps demanding answer in paired images and notes pride/thicket idiom.

12:6|Even your brothers and your father’s household
have betrayed you.
Even they shout after you at full voice.
Do not trust them,
even when they speak kindly to you.|Retains family betrayal and loud cry without adding an unattested mob.

12:7|I have left my house,
abandoned my inheritance.
I have handed the beloved of my soul
over to her enemies.|Keeps divine loss, feminine beloved, and inheritance language.

12:8|My inheritance has become to me
like a lion in the forest.
She has roared against me;
that is why I hate her.|Preserves painful hate language and gendered lion image.

12:9|Is my inheritance a speckled bird of prey,
with birds of prey surrounding her?
Go, gather all the wild animals;
bring them to devour!|Retains uncertain bird image and predatory summons; hyena alternative noted.

12:10|Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard;
they have trampled my plot of land.
They have made my cherished plot
a desolate wilderness.|Keeps shepherd/vineyard mixed imagery and repeated plot.

12:11|It has been made a wasteland;
desolate, it mourns before me.
The whole land lies waste,
because no one takes it to heart.|Keeps land as mourning subject and lack of human attention.

12:12|Destroyers have come
over all the bare heights in the wilderness.
The **LORD** has a sword that devours
from one end of the land to the other.
No flesh has peace.|Retains consuming sword and broad flesh expression.

12:13|They sowed wheat but reaped thorns.
They exhausted themselves but gained nothing.
Be ashamed of your harvests
because of the **LORD**’s burning anger.”|Keeps frustrating harvest and source shift from they to you.

12:14|This is what the **LORD** says about all my evil neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave my people Israel: “Look, I will uproot them from their soil, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.|Preserves God’s own neighbors designation and repeated uprooting of different groups.

12:15|After I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them and bring each back to their own inheritance and their own land.|Keeps compassion and return extended to neighboring peoples, not only Judah.

12:16|If they truly learn my people’s ways and swear by my name, ‘As the **LORD** lives’—just as they taught my people to swear by Baal—they will be built up among my people.|Retains conditional inclusion and reversal of religious teaching.
12:17|But if they do not listen, I will uproot that nation completely and destroy it,” declares the **LORD**.|Keeps conditional threat alongside prior promise without reconciliation.
13:1|This is what the **LORD** said to me: “Go and buy a linen waistcloth. Put it around your waist, but do not put it in water.”|Uses waistcloth for worn linen object and retains water prohibition.
13:2|So I bought the waistcloth as the **LORD** had said and put it around my waist.|Preserves straightforward obedient action and repeated object.
13:3|The **LORD**’s word came to me a second time:|Retains sequence of renewed speech.

13:4|“Take the waistcloth you bought, the one around your waist. Go at once to Perath and hide it there in a crevice in the rock.”|Retains Hebrew place-name rather than silently deciding Euphrates or local site.
13:5|I went and hid it at Perath, as the **LORD** had commanded me.|Keeps repeated location and obedience.
13:6|Many days later, the **LORD** said to me, “Go at once to Perath and get the waistcloth I told you to hide there.”|Preserves indefinite elapsed time and retrieval command.

13:7|I went to Perath, dug up the waistcloth, and took it from the place where I had hidden it. It was ruined—good for nothing.|Keeps excavation and emphatic uselessness without adding an explanation of decay.
13:8|Then the **LORD**’s word came to me:|Retains interpretation introduced as divine speech.
13:9|“This is what the **LORD** says: In the same way, I will ruin Judah’s pride and Jerusalem’s great pride.|Keeps ruin as connection between sign and meaning.

13:10|This evil people refuses to listen to my words. They follow their stubborn hearts and go after other gods to serve and worship them. They will be like this waistcloth, good for nothing.|Retains refusal, pursuit, service/worship, and repeated uselessness.

13:11|As a waistcloth clings to a man’s waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me,” declares the **LORD**, “to be my people, my name, my praise, and my glory. But they would not listen.|Keeps physical closeness, specific man, both houses, and fourfold intended relation.

13:12|“Tell them this: This is what the **LORD**, Israel’s God, says: Every jar will be filled with wine. They will answer, ‘Don’t we know that every jar will be filled with wine?’|Retains seemingly obvious saying and mocking reply before explanation.

13:13|Then tell them: This is what the **LORD** says: Look, I am filling everyone who lives in this land with drunkenness—the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and everyone who lives in Jerusalem.|Preserves all groups and drunkenness as divine filling.

13:14|I will smash them against one another, fathers and sons together,” declares the **LORD**. “No pity, no mercy, no compassion will keep me from destroying them.”|Keeps violent jar metaphor and threefold refusal of pity.
13:15|Listen and pay attention;\ndo not be proud,\nfor the **LORD** has spoken.|Retains paired listening commands and pride connection.

13:16|Give glory to the **LORD** your God
before he brings darkness,
before your feet stumble on the mountains at dusk.
You hope for light,
but he will turn it to deep darkness,
make it thick gloom.|Keeps temporal urgency, stumbling setting, and recorded final verbal connection.

13:17|But if you will not listen,
my soul will weep in secret because of your pride.
My eyes will weep bitterly and stream with tears,
for the **LORD**’s flock has been taken captive.|Preserves concealed grief and shepherd image without merging voice into a narrator.

13:18|Say to the king and the queen mother,
“Take a low seat,
for your glorious crown
has fallen from your heads.”|Retains queen mother’s royal standing and lowered seat/crown image.

13:19|The cities of the Negeb are shut,
with no one to open them.
All Judah has gone into exile,
wholly carried away.|Keeps geographic Negeb and emphatic totality.

13:20|Lift your eyes and see those coming from the north!\nWhere is the flock entrusted to you,\nyour glorious sheep?|Preserves entrustment question; English you accommodates written/read number change.

13:21|What will you say when he sets over you as rulers
those you trained to be your close friends?
Will pain not seize you
like a woman in labor?|Adopts appointment sense with ambiguous clause noted; retains childbirth pain.

13:22|And if you ask yourself,
‘Why has this happened to me?’—
it is because of your great guilt
that your skirts have been stripped back
and your body violated.|Preserves sexual violence implied by exposed skirts and violated heels; note names literal image.

13:23|Can a Cushite change his skin,
or a leopard its spots?
Then you too could do good,
though you are trained in doing evil.|Keeps specific ethnic comparison and sarcastic impossibility without implying dark skin itself is evil.
13:24|“I will scatter them like straw\nblown by a wilderness wind.|Keeps scatter image and third-person them.

13:25|This is your lot,
the portion I have measured out for you,”
declares the **LORD**,
“because you forgot me
and trusted in falsehood.|Preserves measured allotment and forgotten God/false trust pair.
13:26|I myself will strip your skirts up over your face,\nand your shame will be seen.|Retains divine agency and exposure metaphor without euphemizing harm.

13:27|Your adulteries, your lustful neighing,
your shameless prostitution—
on the hills, in the open country,
I have seen your abominations.
Woe to you, Jerusalem!
How much longer before you are clean?”|Keeps animal/sexual imagery and unsettled concluding question.
14:1|The **LORD**’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the droughts:|Retains plural droughts and prophetic heading.

14:2|Judah mourns;
her gates languish.
They sink to the ground in mourning,
and Jerusalem’s cry rises.|Keeps personified gates and downward/upward contrast.

14:3|Her nobles send their servants for water.
They come to the cisterns and find none.
They return with empty jars,
ashamed and humiliated,
their heads covered.|Renders lesser/younger ones as servants in context; retains mourning gesture.

14:4|The ground is cracked,
for no rain has fallen on the land.
The farmers are ashamed;
they cover their heads.|Keeps cause of agricultural collapse and repeated gesture.
14:5|Even a doe in the field gives birth\nand abandons her fawn,\nbecause there is no grass.|Retains animal suffering and reason without moralizing the mother.

14:6|Wild donkeys stand on the bare heights,
panting for air like jackals.
Their eyes fail
because there is no vegetation.|Keeps exact animal comparison and failing eyes.

14:7|Though our wrongs testify against us,
**LORD**, act for your name’s sake.
Our acts of turning away are many;
we have sinned against you.|Keeps confession as basis of plea and recurring turn language.

14:8|Hope of Israel,
its savior in time of trouble,
